title: Lamb Meatballs with Gochujang Glaze + Kabocha Purée (Peanut Crunch)

blocks.text: **Affiliate note:** If you see product links on this site, they may be affiliate links. If you buy through them, I may earn a small commission at no extra cost to you.

I made this on a night where I wanted dinner to feel like a *special occasion* without leaving Montreal or fighting for a reservation. The plan was simple: cook something that looks dramatic, tastes expensive, and still lets you spend most of the night talking instead of panicking.

These **lamb meatballs** are sweet-savory and a little spicy, lacquered in a sticky **gochujang glaze**. They land on a silky **kabocha squash purée** with miso, sake, and mirin (yes, it’s that kind of cozy). Then you hit it with **peanut crunch** so every bite has something to bite back.
It’s the kind of plate that makes someone pause after the first bite. Not because it’s complicated. Because it feels like you meant it.

items: **Big flavor with a clean structure:** meatballs, glaze, purée, crunch.
**Looks restaurant-level** but the steps are mostly repeatable patterns.
**Sweet, spicy, nutty, and creamy** all in one bite.
**Date-night friendly:** you can prep components ahead, then assemble like you’re calm and mysterious.

blocks.text: Shopping Notes (So You Don’t Overthink It)

items: **Kabocha:** Look for a deep green squash with dull skin and a heavy feel. It’s sweet, chestnutty, and makes purée taste naturally rich.

**Perilla oil + seeds:** If you have them, use them. If you don’t, you can still make a great crunch with sesame oil + sesame seeds. (But perilla is a little more “what *is* that flavor?” in the best way.)
**Lamb:** Ground lamb can vary in fattiness. If yours is very lean, a small drizzle of oil in the mix helps keep meatballs juicy.
**Garlic + ginger amounts:** These are bold by design. It’s date-night food, not background music.
Heat 2 tbsp canola oil in a small pot over medium heat.
Add diced kabocha. Cook 3–4 minutes to get it coated and lightly golden in spots.
Add miso, sake, and mirin. Stir, bring to a simmer, then cover and cook until kabocha is very tender, about 12–15 minutes.
Uncover and simmer 2–3 minutes to reduce slightly.
Blend until completely smooth. (If needed, add a small splash of water to loosen.)

blocks.text: **Texture goal:** silky enough to swipe with a spoon, thick enough to hold meatballs on top.

items: In a small pan over medium heat, toast peanuts until they smell like peanut butter, 3–5 minutes.
Add sugar and stir until it melts and coats the peanuts.
Stir in perilla seeds, perilla oil, and salt.
Spread on a plate to cool, then chop into a crunchy rubble.

blocks.text: **Tip:** Do not walk away when sugar is in the pan. It goes from “perfect” to “why does it taste like campfire” fast.

items: Heat 1 tbsp canola oil in a small pot.
Add garlic and ginger and cook 30–60 seconds until fragrant.
Add coriander and cumin. Stir 15 seconds.
Add hoisin, gochujang, sake, and sherry vinegar.
Simmer 8–12 minutes until glossy and slightly thick.

blocks.text: **Consistency check:** It should coat the back of a spoon and leave a clean line when you drag your finger through.
4) Make and cook the lamb meatballs

items: In a bowl, combine ground lamb, brown sugar, garlic, ginger, soy sauce, mint, cilantro, and gochugaru.
Mix gently until combined. Don’t overwork it.
Form meatballs in whatever size you want.
Smaller meatballs feel more snacky and “shared plate” friendly.
Larger meatballs feel more main-character and dinner-plate worthy.
Heat 2 tbsp canola oil in a skillet over medium-high heat.
Brown meatballs on all sides, then lower heat to medium and cook until done, about 8–10 minutes total depending on size.
Toss hot meatballs in the gochujang glaze.
Spoon a swoosh of kabocha purée onto each plate.

blocks.text: During the Date (What to Do While Things Simmer)
This recipe has built-in little pauses. Use them.

items: **While the kabocha cooks:** rinse herbs, put on music, and decide what you’re drinking.
**Two-person prep split:** one person rolls meatballs, one person makes the glaze. You’ll finish faster and it feels like you’re cooking *together*.
**Taste test moment:** dip a spoon into the glaze and ask, “More heat, or are we being nice tonight?”
**Plate together:** let your date sprinkle the peanut crunch and herbs at the table. It’s small, it’s interactive, and it makes the dish feel collaborative.
**Keep the purée warm** (low heat with a lid) so plating feels smooth and effortless.
**Glaze at the end.** If you glaze too early and keep cooking, you can burn the sugars.
**Herbs are not decoration.** They are the fresh, green counterbalance that keeps the whole plate from feeling heavy.

blocks.text: Yes. Make the purée and glaze ahead. Reheat gently. Cook meatballs fresh, then glaze and assemble.
**What if I can’t find perilla oil?**
Use toasted sesame oil for the crunch. It will be different, but still delicious.
It’s sweet-first, then warm heat. Adjust by using less gochujang or adding a little more hoisin.
**Lamb Meatballs with Gochujang Glaze + Kabocha Purée (Peanut Crunch)**

items: 8 oz kabocha squash, peeled and diced

blocks.text: **Lamb Meatballs (Yield: as many as you like)**

items: ½ cup herb mix (mint, cilantro, Thai basil)
Simmer kabocha with miso, sake, mirin until tender. Blend smooth.
Make peanut crunch: toast peanuts, caramelize lightly with sugar, stir in perilla seeds/oil + salt. Cool and chop.
Make glaze: sauté garlic/ginger + spices, simmer with hoisin, gochujang, sake, vinegar until glossy.
Mix and form lamb meatballs to your preferred size. Pan-brown and cook through.
Toss meatballs in glaze. Plate over purée. Top with crunch + herbs.
